title: Nightshift ops scratchbox - mika
content:
— quick morning checklist (nightshift)
- 04:30 wake up, coffee, check ops dashboard
- Look at pool health: prod-gpu-pool-a / prod-gpu-pool-b / edge-test-pool
  - metric to watch: queue length > 12 -> escalate
  - if p50 latency spikes > 300ms, toggle routing to standby region
- Immediate triage steps:
  - run `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu` -> spot NotReady
  - if single node flapping: cordon + drain with --ignore-daemonsets; annotate: `kubectl annotate node <node> shift/evacuate=yes`
  - use `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv` to check thermal
  - nvtop for a live view if remote session open
- Capacity TODOs:
  - reclaim candidates list (low utilization > 72h): node-ux-12, node-ux-13, node-edge-03
  - open ticket INFRA-2401 for reclaim scheduling; propose batch drain windows Tue/Thu 03:00-05:00 UTC
  - follow up with capacity-team: can we bump burst pool by +2 T4s next quarter?
- Networking reminders:
  - check BGP sessions toward DC-east (iffy since 03:20 UTC last night) — watch for flaps
  - if flapping, run `show ip bgp summary` on jumpbox -> escalate to network-team
  - temp L3 workaround: add static route to fallthrough for zone edge ~ beware of traffic asymmetry
- Ongoing tasks (quick bullets):
  - finish small patch to autoscaler: fix scaleDownCooldown bug (PR link above)
  - test small batching config change on canary: decrease max_batch_delay from 30ms -> 20ms
  - run perf job against rtv-model-003 with seq_len=512 to validate latency impact
- Notes to self:
  - metric alert INF-CPU-HT gone off twice at 02:10 -> check oomkilled pods history
  - investigate repeated preemptions on spot nodes (cloud provider logs attached in ticket)
  - remind Ben in morning to review the dedicated pool pricing estimate
- Quick commands I keep here (copy-paste):
  - kubectl cordon <node>
  - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  - kubectl uncordon <node>
  - watch -n 5 'kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide | grep Evicted'
  - gcloud compute instances reset <instance-id> --zone=<zone>
- Decision checkpoints:
  - if queue length > 20 and scaling not keeping up -> engage autoscaler dev oncall (pager)
  - if rolling drain fails on > 3 nodes concurrently -> abort and rollback, open postmortem stub
- Open questions / unresolved:
  - should we change draining policy to prefer evicting preemptible first? pros/cons
  - where to store the list of reclaim candidates centrally? currently scattered in sheets
  - can we get a nightly job that reconciles low-util GPUs and creates reclaim PR automatically?
- Closing notes:
  - 06:10: looks quieter, queue down from 18 -> 6, started canary batch change
  - leave note on #sre-nightops: brief summary + link to this doc
  - follow ups: PR review ping, schedule reclaim planning sync (30m)

---
Rough timeline log (timestamps local):
- 04:35 checked dashboards, prod queue 18
- 04:41 cordoned node node-ux-12, started drain
- 05:02 noticed BGP flaps; pinged network-team (Evan)
- 05:15 canary config rolled; p50 latency dropped by ~40ms on canary instances
- 05:45 autoscaler did not scale to burst; created INFRA-2345

End quick scratchbox — add to cleanup list later.
